bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: The J2K codestream parser materializes code-block geometry and per-tile/component `cblksty` values from `SPCod`/`SPCoc`. The saved witness later drives one `opj_t1_clbl_decode_processor` job through the HT decoder and another through the classic decoder on the same thread-local `opj_t1_t`. In `src/lib/openjp2/ht_dec.c`, `opj_t1_allocate_buffers()` computes `flagssize == 2640` for the HT scratch layout and allocates only `flagssize` bytes for `t1->flags`, but also stores `t1->flagssize = 2640` in a field that `src/lib/openjp2/t1.c` interprets as a count of `opj_flag_t` elements. When the later classic codeblock computes `flagssize == 957` elements, `if (flagssize > t1->flagssize)` is false against the stale 2640 value, so no reallocation occurs and `memset(t1->flags, 0, flagssize * sizeof(opj_flag_t))` writes 3828 bytes into the earlier 2640-byte HT allocation. AddressSanitizer records the overflow at `t1.c:1504` and the allocation at `ht_dec.c:1066`. The fix multiplies the HT allocation and clear sizes by `sizeof(opj_flag_t)`, making the shared `t1->flagssize` state consistent with the actual buffer size.

source.description: First project parser statement that consumes attacker-controlled codestream bytes and materializes the code-block width/height exponents later used to derive the decoded codeblock rectangle and the classic allocator's `flagssize`.
source.value_from: `gt_results/arvo_47500/poc` is a 1479-byte JPEG 2000 codestream (SHA-256 `a8c206bdf138579b29eb1b03bc5a1c8b4af741cd7b40db9a543948abbdf88ac9`). `opj_j2k_read_SPCod_SPCoc()` consumes its `SPCod`/`SPCoc` bytes directly into `l_tccp->cblkw`, `l_tccp->cblkh`, and later `l_tccp->cblksty`; the saved ASan allocation stack from `ht_dec.c` and crash stack from `t1.c` show the resulting parsed state drives both the HT and classic Tier-1 paths.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The classic Tier-1 allocator clears `flagssize * sizeof(opj_flag_t)` bytes through `t1->flags` after reusing the undersized HT allocation, overflowing the heap buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `WRITE of size 3828` at this line, which matches the classic allocator writing 957 `opj_flag_t` elements into the earlier 2640-byte HT allocation.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The HT decoder allocates only `flagssize` raw bytes for `t1->flags` while later storing the same numeric `flagssize` into shared field `t1->flagssize`, which the classic decoder interprets as a count of `opj_flag_t` elements.
root_cause.note: Here `flagssize` is 2640 bytes of HT scratch space, but `opj_t1_t.flagssize` is later compared against classic element counts. The fix keeps `t1->flagssize = 2640` but changes the HT allocation and clear to `flagssize * sizeof(opj_flag_t)`, making the shared size state conservative for later classic reuse.

tainted_value_origin.description: The codestream's `SPCod`/`SPCoc` style byte is the attacker-controlled dispatch key that later selects HT versus classic Tier-1 decode paths.

parser_admitted.description: After the fuzz target has created the JPEG 2000 stream and decode structures, project code enters the J2K decoder here; subsequent parsing reaches `opj_j2k_read_SPCod_SPCoc()` and later the Tier-1 code-block decode path.

coarse_trace.summary: The codestream parser reads code-block geometry exponents and code-block style bytes from `SPCod`/`SPCoc`, creating the `cblkw`/`cblkh` geometry state and the per-job `cblksty` dispatch state used later by Tier-1 decode.
OpenJPEG materializes each decode-side codeblock's `x0/y0/x1/y1` rectangle from the parsed geometry parameters; later HT and classic allocators derive `w` and `h` from those bounds.
A thread-local `opj_t1_t` handle is reused across codeblock jobs. One parsed `cblksty` takes the HT branch and another later job on the same TLS object takes the classic branch.

The HT allocator computes a 2640-byte scratch layout, allocates only that many bytes for `t1->flags`, and stores `t1->flagssize = 2640` on the shared `opj_t1_t`, even though the classic allocator interprets that field as an element count.

During the later classic decode, `flagssize` is recomputed from the current codeblock dimensions, the stale `t1->flagssize = 2640` suppresses reallocation, and `memset(..., flagssize * sizeof(opj_flag_t))` overruns the earlier HT allocation.

fine_trace.note: Source. `SPCod`/`SPCoc` bytes from the attacker-controlled J2K codestream are decoded into the code-block width and height exponents. Those exponents later determine the decode-side `cblk->x0..y1` rectangle and therefore the classic allocator's `w`, `h`, and `flagssize`.

This parser statement materializes the per-tile/component code-block style byte. The nearby `HTMIXED` rejection proves the witness stays on supported styles; the saved allocation and crash stacks prove the resulting parsed `cblksty` values later include both an HT job and a non-HT job, which is the dispatch difference needed for the cross-path reuse.

fine_trace.code: l_code_block->x0 = opj_int_max(cblkxstart, l_current_precinct->x0); l_code_block->y0 = opj_int_max(cblkystart, l_current_precinct->y0); l_code_block->x1 = opj_int_min(cblkxend, l_current_precinct->x1); l_code_block->y1 = opj_int_min(cblkyend, l_current_precinct->y1);
fine_trace.note: For each decode-side codeblock, OpenJPEG materializes the clipped rectangle that later allocators use. Both HT and classic Tier-1 paths derive `w = cblk->x1 - cblk->x0` and `h = cblk->y1 - cblk->y0` from these fields.

fine_trace.code: t1 = (opj_t1_t*) opj_tls_get(tls, OPJ_TLS_KEY_T1); if ((tccp->cblksty & J2K_CCP_CBLKSTY_HT) != 0) { if (OPJ_FALSE == opj_t1_ht_decode_cblk(...)) { ... } }
fine_trace.note: The decoder keeps one `opj_t1_t` per worker thread in TLS. For an HT-coded job, the parsed `cblksty` takes the HT branch and sends that shared `t1` object into `opj_t1_ht_decode_cblk()`. Because the handle lives in TLS rather than per job, its `flags` pointer and `flagssize` state can persist into later codeblock jobs on the same thread.

fine_trace.code: flagssize = 132U * sizeof(OPJ_UINT32) * 4U; flagssize += 528U; if (flagssize > t1->flagssize) { opj_aligned_free(t1->flags); t1->flags = (opj_flag_t*) opj_aligned_malloc(flagssize); } t1->flagssize = flagssize;
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The HT scratch layout needs 4 arrays of 132 `OPJ_UINT32`s (2112 bytes) plus 528 bytes of line-state storage, so this code computes a raw-byte footprint of 2640. The vulnerable line allocates exactly 2640 bytes for `t1->flags` and then stores `t1->flagssize = 2640` on the shared `opj_t1_t`. Later classic code interprets that field as 2640 `opj_flag_t` elements, so the recorded shared size state is four times larger than the actual allocation.

fine_trace.code: } else { if (OPJ_FALSE == opj_t1_decode_cblk(t1, cblk, band->bandno, (OPJ_UINT32)tccp->roishift, tccp->cblksty, job->p_manager, job->p_manager_mutex, job->check_pterm)) { ... } }
fine_trace.note: A later codeblock job on the same worker reuses the existing TLS `t1`, but its parsed `cblksty` does not take the HT branch, so the same `t1->flags` pointer and stale `t1->flagssize` state are handed to the classic Tier-1 decoder. The saved ASan allocation and crash stacks both pass through this dispatcher, which is the source-level evidence for the HT-to-classic handoff.

fine_trace.code: flags_stride = w + 2U; flagssize = (h + 3U) / 4U + 2U; flagssize *= flags_stride; if (flagssize > t1->flagssize) { opj_aligned_free(t1->flags); t1->flags = (opj_flag_t*) opj_aligned_malloc(flagssize * sizeof(opj_flag_t)); } t1->flagssize = flagssize;
fine_trace.note: The classic allocator derives an element-count `flagssize` from the current codeblock dimensions `w` and `h`. For the crashing job, ASan reports `WRITE of size 3828` at the next line; because `opj_flag_t` is `OPJ_UINT32`, that means this call reached the sink with `flagssize == 957` elements. The guard `if (flagssize > t1->flagssize)` is therefore false against the stale HT value `t1->flagssize == 2640`, so no reallocation happens even though the actual buffer from step 5 is only 2640 bytes long.

ASan sink. The classic path clears `957 * 4 = 3828` bytes through `t1->flags`, but that pointer still refers to the 2640-byte allocation created by the HT path in step 5, so the write runs immediately off the right edge of the heap region exactly as recorded.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the overflowed region was allocated earlier by the HT decoder's `opj_t1_allocate_buffers()` call at line 1066.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, reproduction_report.json, patch.diff, and the preserved vulnerable source tree

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. ASan's allocation stack points to the HT allocator line that reserves only 2640 bytes for `t1->flags`; that undersized HT allocation is exactly the shared-state bug that later makes the classic `memset` overflow.
cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch changes the HT allocator and HT `memset` to use `flagssize * sizeof(opj_flag_t)`, so the shared `t1->flagssize = 2640` now corresponds to enough memory for any later classic `flagssize * sizeof(opj_flag_t)` clear on the saved witness.

poc.trigger: The staged 1479-byte witness is a JPEG 2000 codestream. The saved vulnerable run proves that it parses `SPCod`/`SPCoc` state that drives one `opj_t1_clbl_decode_processor` job through `opj_t1_ht_decode_cblk -> ht_dec.c::opj_t1_allocate_buffers`, leaving a 2640-byte `t1->flags` allocation, and later drives another job on the same TLS `opj_t1_t` through `opj_t1_decode_cblk -> t1.c::opj_t1_allocate_buffers`, whose `memset(..., 3828)` overflows that earlier allocation.

format.name: 1479-byte JPEG 2000 codestream for `opj_decompress_fuzzer_J2K`
format.contract: Exactly the staged witness file `gt_results/arvo_47500/poc` with SHA-256 `a8c206bdf138579b29eb1b03bc5a1c8b4af741cd7b40db9a543948abbdf88ac9`. The saved ASan artifacts prove only these trigger semantics: the codestream is accepted far enough for `opj_j2k_read_SPCod_SPCoc()` and later Tier-1 decode, it causes at least one HT codeblock decode and a later classic codeblock decode on the same thread-local `opj_t1_t`, and the classic allocator then clears 3828 bytes into the 2640-byte `t1->flags` allocation created earlier by the HT allocator. The staged artifacts do not identify the exact marker bytes or tile/component sequence responsible for the HT-to-classic transition, so this contract is intentionally limited to the exact witness and observed cross-path reuse.
